reply.thought: Before any payout I must confirm the refunds table matches Alpha's report. W2 says order 194 was not recorded, so I'll check the table directly rather than rely on the handoff summary.
The refunds table matches W2's report: 192 and 193 are present and 194 is absent, as reported. The refunds check passes, so I can move on. Next I need the customer list, so I'll fetch the orders.
The refunds table matches Alpha's report, so I can proceed. The orders list has three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
The acme net balance of 33841 matches the order total (32343 + 11079 = 43422) less refund 193 (9581). Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance of 40664 matches its orders (26465 + 14199 = 40664) with no refunds applied to birch. Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll fetch its net balance.

All three net balances match the order totals less the applied refunds. But W2 reports refund 194 (5972 cents, birch's order) failed and is not in the ledger. Birch's net is therefore likely overstated by that amount, and payouts cannot be recalled. I'll hold the batch for review rather than pay.
